title: Google DeepMind, robotik yapay zeka platformu Gemini Robotics 2.5 sürümünü duyurdu
summary: Google DeepMind, fiziksel beceri ve gerçek dünya güvenilirliğini artıran yeni nesil Gemini Robotics 2.5 platformunu tanıttı.
body:
Google DeepMind'ın duyurusuna göre, yeni nesil **Gemini Robotics 2.5** platformu gerçek dünyadaki görevleri insan seviyesine daha da yaklaştırıyor. 9 Kasım'da yayımlanan resmi açıklama ve Ars Technica'nın aktardığı detaylara göre, platformun gelişiminde **Gemini 4 Argon** modeli simülasyon motoru olarak kritik bir rol oynadı.

## Gemini Robotics 2.5 yenilikleri neler?

Platform, kullanıcı talimatlarını canlı video ile planlayan Gemini Embodied Reasoning ile robot eylemlerini oluşturan Gemini Robotics bileşenlerinden oluşuyor. Ars Technica'nın haberine göre model; maşayla yemek servis etmek ve laboratuvarda pipet kullanmak dahil 200'den fazla etkinlikte değerlendirildi. Apptronik'in Apollo 2 insansı robotu, beş parmaklı elleriyle kurdele bağlama gibi zorlu becerileri bu sürümle birlikte başarıyla gerçekleştirebiliyor. Laboratuvar testlerinde önceki sürüme göre %30 ila %100 daha yüksek başarı oranı sunan model, %20 ila %30 oranında daha hızlı çalışıyor.

## Fabrika testleri ve gerçek dünya performansı

Google; Agile, Apptronik ve Mercedes-Benz ortaklığıyla sistemin laboratuvar dışındaki performansını da test etti. Gemini destekli Apollo 2 robotları, bazı Avrupa fabrikalarında otomotiv parçalarını dizerek %96 başarı oranına ulaştı. DeepMind direktörü Kanishka Rao, insan seviyesindeki kusursuz tekrara ulaşmak için kalan %4'lük boşluğun aşılmasının zorlu bir yol olacağını belirtti. Geliştirme sürecinde Gemini 4 Argon, gerçek dünya kamera sahnelerinden binlerce simüle edilmiş pratik çalışması üreterek robotların yeni sahnelere daha hızlı adapte olmasını sağladı.

**Neden önemli?** Gemini Robotics 2.5, robotların insanlarla birlikte çalışarak gerçek dünya zorluklarını çözebilmesi adına fiziksel yapay zekanın geliştirilmesinde önemli bir kilometre taşı oluşturuyor.

source_texts.title: Gemini Robotics 2.5 accelerates real-world general dexterity
source_texts.summary: Our most capable vision-language-action model enhances robot dexterity, reliability, and safety
source_texts.text:
To teach robots new skills, researchers need massive amounts of physical data and highly efficient modelling algorithms. Gemini 4 Argon’s robotics research capabilities helped solve these bottlenecks by acting as a simulation engine, which greatly accelerated our development of Gemini Robotics 2.5.
Argon can generate thousands of varied, simulated practice runs from a real-world camera scene and build a realistic digital twin. Combined with real training demonstrations, this enables the robot to more quickly generalize to new scenes and objects. Argon can also help researchers hypothesize why task failures happen from video footage and test the best improvements both in simulation and directly on real robots.
Accelerated by frontier intelligence models like Gemini 4 Argon, Gemini Robotics 2.5 marks an important milestone on the path toward solving physical AGI. By advancing in dexterity, real-world reliability, and rigorous safety, we are building the physical intelligence necessary for robots to work alongside people and solve real-world challenges

Finally, we’d like to thank our partners: Agile, Apptronik, and Mercedes-Benz teams for their support on this release.

source_texts.text:
Google DeepMind has revealed a new generation of the AI-powered Gemini Robotics platform. In the 2.5 release, Google says its robotic AI is getting tantalizingly close to completing real-world tasks as well as humans do. In fact, some Gemini robots were able to get actual work done in Mercedes-Benz factories, and the team is preparing for a day when robots operate alongside humans with an open source safety benchmark.
DeepMind’s physical AI platform has several computational layers between user input and robotic action. There’s the vision-language model piece, which is Gemini Embodied Reasoning. Essentially, it takes your instructions and uses live video to plan how the robot can accomplish the task. The other main component is the vision-language-action (VLA) that actually generates robot actions, like moving an actuator—that’s Gemini Robotics, which has been bumped to version 2.5.
DeepMind says that Gemini Robotics 2.5 is much better at tasks that require a high degree of dexterity. The model was evaluated across more than 200 activities, including serving food with tongs and using a pipette, as you would see in a laboratory. Google also showed that Apptronik’s Apollo 2 humanoid robot with Gemini Robotics 2.5 can now tie a bow with its five-fingered hands, a notable feat, because deformable objects (like ribbon) are notoriously difficult for robots to manipulate.
Overall, Gemini Robotics 2.5 manages a 30 to 100 percent higher success rate compared to the last version. It’s also 20 to 30 percent faster. But that’s based on laboratory testing. Google partnered with Apptronik and Mercedes-Benz to see how capable this AI is when faced with the uncertainty of the world outside robotics labs. The Gemini-powered Apollo 2 robots kitted automotive parts in a few European factories, reaching a 96 percent success rate.
That’s an impressive showing compared to previous robotic AI systems, but it’s still probably not enough for a company like Mercedes-Benz. A human doing that sort of repetitive task will get it right virtually every time, and DeepMind director Kanishka Rao notes that closing that last 4 percent gap will be a “steep road.”
